comparisons.peer_summary: The firm calculates the fair value of financial liabilities subject to the fair value option by discounting future cash flows at a rate that incorporates the firm's credit spreads.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs describe calculating the fair value of financial liabilities subject to the fair value option by incorporating firm-specific credit spreads. Citi states it uses observed bond market credit spreads to determine the change in fair value related to its own credit, which is then presented in AOCI. Goldman Sachs similarly calculates fair value by discounting future cash flows using a rate that incorporates its credit spreads. While Citi explicitly details the segregation of these changes into AOCI in the summary text provided, Goldman Sachs focuses on the calculation methodology itself in this specific disclosure, noting in other disclosures that such DVA gains/losses are included in revenue (though this specific sentence only mentions calculation).

sentences.text: Citi presents separately in AOCI the portion of the total change in the fair value of a liability resulting from a change in the instrument-specific credit risk, when management has elected to measure the liability at fair value in accordance with the fair value option for financial instruments.
Accordingly, the change in fair value of liabilities for which the fair value option was elected related to changes in Citigroup's own credit spreads is presented in AOCI.
The firm calculates the fair value of financial liabilities for which the fair value option is elected by discounting future cash flows at a rate which incorporates the firm's credit spreads.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting Treatment of DVA and Materiality of Realized Gains
comparisons.peer_summary: Unrealized gains or losses due to instrument-specific credit risk (DVA) for elected liabilities are recorded in OCI, while realized gains or losses are recorded in principal transactions revenue. Realized gains or losses from instrument-specific credit risk were not material for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan disclose the specific accounting treatment for unrealized gains or losses due to instrument-specific credit risk (DVA) on liabilities where the fair value option is elected. Both firms present these unrealized credit risk changes in Other Comprehensive Income (Citi specifies Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income, JPM specifies OCI). Citi explains this is to separate the portion of fair value change resulting from instrument-specific credit risk from other changes. JPMorgan confirms that unrealized DVA for elected liabilities is recorded in OCI, while realized gains/losses go to revenue.
